units.title: Lecture 2 - Manual Muscle Testing (MMT)
units.summary: Functional Movement Science (HAS4867) Manual Muscle Testing (MMT) Manual muscle testing is a procedure for the evaluation of the strength of individual muscles and muscle groups based on the performance of a movement in relation to manual resistance. Patients are asked to hold a position against a therapist’s resistance. Resistance needs to be applied gradually in the opposite direction of muscle being tested. Both sides should be tested to provide a comparison. Muscle Strength Grading Scale (Oxford Scale) • Grade 0: No contraction • Grade1: Visible/palpable muscle contraction but no movement • Grade2: Completes ROM with gravity eliminated • Grade 3: Completes ROM against gravity only • Grade 4: Completes ROM against gravity with some resistance • Grade 5: Completes ROM against gravity with full resistance Testing position • Anti-Gravity – for muscle strength Grade 3 or above • Gravity Eliminated – for muscle strength Grade 2 or below

Shoulder Extension Subject Test Position Prone lying with arm by the side, palm facing up Action Ask the subject to extend arm to end range, and hold the position against therapist’s manual resistance Examiner’s Resistance Examiner stabilizes the subject’s scapula and gives the resistance above the elbow Gravity Eliminated Position Side lying with the testing arm supported by the examiner, and check the subject whether he/she can do a full ROM or not (Grade 2) 3. Shoulder Abduction Subject Test Position Sitting with arm by the side Action Ask the subject to abduct arm up to 90° with palm facing down, and hold the position against therapist’s manual resistance Examiner’s Resistance Examiner stabilizes the subject’s scapula and gives the resistance above the elbow Gravity Eliminated Position Supine lying with the testing arm supported by the bed, and check the subject whether he/she can do a full ROM or not (Grade 2) 4.
